task: Core #1186 F6-U03b: guarded occupied Fresh Install recovery and atomic customer baseline proof, no automatic execution

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This unit creates the only reviewed path toward deleting and reconstructing a disposable hosted application schema, so critical-tier negative proof, exact source integrity and true transaction rollback must be demonstrated. Existing quality guards only establish the implementation contract; independent hosted target and behavioral proof remain required. Failure or uncertainty must block rather than relax identity and data constraints.

acceptanceCriteria: An opt-in reset can target only project istjjkdcvsvilrycqecd with explicit manual dispatch input and validated PostgreSQL connection authority; all ordinary runs remain non-destructive.
Object, data, Auth, Storage and cross-schema dependency preconditions are checked immediately inside the same database transaction as any cleanup, under serialization, and any uncertainty blocks.
All 59 exact reviewed migration files and canonical Auth bootstrap, neutral seed, clean target preflight and postflight are applied and validated in the same transaction before COMMIT.
At least one integration rollback test confirms failed migration/restore cannot leave an empty or partially installed application schema after a canceled transaction.
Structured evidence reports precise project ref, reviewed source identity, expected and observed schema fingerprints, cleanup intent, applied files and rollback/commit state without leaking secrets.
The workflow and tests reject all fake provenance, unauthorized Storage deletion, unexpected business rows and attempted changes to non-disposable projects.
invariants: Platform and staging project state and databases are never touched, even if supplied credentials or variables point to either project.
Only the known disposable application's public/private owned objects are eligible for reset, and no Supabase-managed schema object may be deleted.
An unknown or nonneutral record, authenticated user, Storage object, migration-history row or managed-schema dependency blocks destructive execution.
Any destructive SQL and its canonical migration replay remain in one database transaction; COMMIT occurs only after postflight PASS.
No source-only review, CI PASS, postflight simulation or old historical 0046 proof can masquerade as F6-U03b hosted deployment proof.
forbiddenStates: Schema cleanup committed without the 59 migrations and postflight completing successfully.
Any destructive action triggered by a push or pull request or absent an exact manual opt-in bound to the disposable target.
Direct deletion of storage.objects, storage.buckets or auth managed user/session metadata through SQL.
Undetected cross-schema dependency cascade against unrelated auth, storage, realtime or platform extensions.
Project identity derived exclusively from untrusted URL text or inherited PGHOSTADDR/PGSERVICE selectors.
Publishing READY or merging an unverified destructive workflow before fault-injection proof and exact-head Completion Truth.

failureModes: Wrong connection environment or pooler login silently selects platform instead of the dedicated disposable database.
The target acquired commerce/user rows since the last read-only inventory and the reset removes customer data.
DROP SCHEMA public/private CASCADE removes Auth hooks and privileges outside the intended application authority.
Existing four Storage bucket upserts are treated as a virgin provider environment and create false postflight confidence.
A later migration fails and the runner commits an empty or half-created database due to shell or psql transaction errors.
A second concurrent proof run or web traffic changes schema/data in the window between guard and cleanup.
A Git checkout contains modified 0058 SQL while file names are unchanged and an unreviewed chain executes.
An external process timeout kills psql after COMMIT without trusted evidence of the final target state.
edgeCases: Exactly seven known neutral entitlement catalogs contain 113 rows while all other 170 application tables have zero.
Auth.users has a single known public/private-dependent trigger and Storage has exactly four known empty buckets.
An extension-owned public object or an unexpected foreign key from a managed schema appears after catalog snapshot.
PostgreSQL transaction fails at migration 0001, corrected 0058, Auth bootstrap, neutral seed or target postflight.
Connection attempt carries PGOPTIONS, PGHOSTADDR, PGSERVICE, sslmode=require or an unapproved pooler host.
A reviewed migration contains a psql meta-command, an extra 0060 SQL file, or missing customer-baseline companion.
RLS and grants recreated in a freshly created public schema differ from the original Supabase schema defaults.
Pooler session mode, TLS CA rotation or role permissions prevent the same-connection transaction protocol.

alternatives.summary: Use opt-in manual guarded reprovision added to the existing Fresh Install proof workflow with one transactional Postgres connection.
alternatives.reason: Preserves one authoritative workflow, exact-source evidence and transactional rollback while keeping the project allowlist and provider-managed schemas intact.

alternatives.summary: Run generic linked Supabase db reset or unrestricted DROP SCHEMA CASCADE on the existing hosted target.
alternatives.reason: Could select historical migrations or delete managed/auth-related dependencies without precise provenance, rollback and provider-state guarantees.

alternatives.summary: Create or activate a separate Supabase project to avoid cleaning the disposable existing test schema.
alternatives.reason: Conflicts with the existing two-active-project budget arrangement and needlessly creates billing and operational complexity.

specialistReviews.finding: Using the repository database secret with any manual workflow is too permissive unless the target is cryptographically bound and all routing/TLS redirects are rejected.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use dedicated target-scoped connection policy, exact ref confirmation, TLS certificate checks and no automatic destructive event path; retain human execution authority.

specialistReviews.finding: An occupied database could accumulate rows or cross-schema dependencies without changing its superficial table and policy counts.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require transactional full schema fingerprint, seven neutral catalog row hashes, every table count and external dependent-object enumeration; stop on drift.

specialistReviews.finding: Postgres one-session atomic DDL may still change non-database Storage state or lose client certainty when the connection drops near commit.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep provider-managed buckets intact, avoid Storage API writes, and classify uncertain commit results as UNKNOWN until an independent postflight.

specialistReviews.finding: Exact Git-reviewed 59-file source parity and quality CI do not by themselves constitute hosted Fresh Install actor and RLS evidence.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep schema proof, live postflight, human PO acceptance, tenant Alap/Pro RLS and provider delivery as distinct required gates and evidence producers.

specialistReviews.finding: Adding another deploy runner rather than extending the canonical workflow risks conflicting Completion Truth and replay evidence ownership.
specialistReviews.resolution: Extend current Fresh Install workflow behind opt-in and use existing Knowledge/Atlas/Failure Intake and exact-head evidence semantics.

challenge.scenario: The exact connection URL looks disposable but PGHOSTADDR or a pooler selector redirects the child process.
challenge.finding: Lexical URL equality cannot prove live endpoint binding when inherited libpq selectors override its effective target.
challenge.resolution: Reuse F6-U03a minimal environment and validated TLS target, reject redirects and verify endpoint before issuing any DDL.

challenge.scenario: An unrelated customer record appears after the previous read-only inventory but before the destructive transaction.
challenge.finding: Past zero-row evidence is stale and cannot authorize deleting an app schema that now stores user data.
challenge.resolution: Re-read exact catalog and every application row count inside the locked transaction, rejecting any nonneutral row or hash drift.

challenge.scenario: A new cross-schema trigger or managed-schema foreign key depends on a public/private application function or table.
challenge.finding: Dropping those schemas may cascade beyond the intended isolated app objects and remove provider dependencies.
challenge.resolution: Enumerate and allowlist only known Auth bootstrap dependencies; fail closed on any unrecognized managed-schema dependent object.

challenge.scenario: A failure at migration 0058 leaves earlier SQL already executed against the freshly cleared schema.
challenge.finding: Without one Postgres session and explicit error stopping, DDL may commit while later baseline replay fails.
challenge.resolution: Wrap cleanup, clean-target preflight, all migration SQL, bootstrap, seed and postflight in one BEGIN/COMMIT with ON_ERROR_STOP; prove ROLLBACK in fault tests.

challenge.scenario: A concurrent proof invocation runs while the first reset is already inspecting or reconstructing application objects.
challenge.finding: Concurrent target mutations can make object counts stale and deadlock or invalidate the guarded assumption.
challenge.resolution: Take an advisory transaction lock and bounded lock/statement timeouts, aborting immediately if exclusive proof ownership is unavailable.

challenge.scenario: An attacker changes historical 0058 migration bytes while preserving the documented 59-file name sequence.
challenge.finding: A migration count alone cannot establish trusted source correctness, and changed policy logic can compromise Alap/Pro roles.
challenge.resolution: Require exact approved F6-U02 Git blob identities and review contract from the already proven F6-U03a source verifier before any reset.

challenge.scenario: Existing managed Storage bucket metadata differs or contains an uploaded file despite application tables being empty.
challenge.finding: The canonical baseline SQL contains Storage bucket upserts, but direct SQL Storage cleanup would violate provider API authority.
challenge.resolution: Require exactly four known empty buckets and zero upload/upload-session objects; refuse SQL deletion of any Storage row or unrelated bucket.

challenge.scenario: A push/pull-request event or routine manual proof with no exact target confirmation attempts to execute DROP SCHEMA.
challenge.finding: An improperly wired workflow input could activate destructive reset using a shared stored database secret.
challenge.resolution: Make guarded reprovision manual opt-in with explicit exact target/project confirmation and separate workflow condition; default mode remains empty-target proof.

challenge.scenario: The transaction succeeds but the client loses connection just after commit and reports no exact outcome artifact.
challenge.finding: A missing terminal log does not justify assuming either rollback or successful canonical deployment.
challenge.resolution: Return UNKNOWN/BLOCKED; require independent read-only postflight and exact-head source lineage before any READY claim.

proofPlan: Require new F6-U03b canonical Development Guard/Plan Before Code PASS from exact inherited F6-U03a closure SHA and all required authority/known-failure mappings.
Show default dry-run/ordinary workflow modes cannot invoke destructive SQL under every relevant GitHub event and input combination.
Run adversarial source tamper, project identity, PG environment, neutral catalog hash, tenant/commerce data, Auth, Storage and cross-schema dependency negative tests.
Exercise real PostgreSQL transaction rollback using disposable offline instances or fault-injection fixtures at preflight, migrations, bootstrap, seed and postflight stages.
Verify exact 59 migration ordering, checked Auth restoration, no partial commit and independent read-only target postflight under trusted TLS.
Record branch+commit+run scoped result, no secrets, verified project identity and explicit limits distinguishing DB schema replay from full provider fresh-state proof.
Require exact-head quality tests, TypeScript, production build, Completion Truth, Lifecycle closure and the existing Future hosted schema/actor proof before READY.
operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The dedicated disposable Shoperation Fresh Install target still contains the previous 0046 customer-baseline PostgreSQL schema, while the canonical 59-migration proof requires an empty application target. Blind migration replay or arbitrary schema reset could destroy unknown data or damage Supabase-managed Auth/Storage state. Build a guarded, explicit, fully rollback-capable reprovision process without a parallel proof authority.
observableOutcomes: An ordinary push, pull request or scheduled build cannot invoke any destructive SQL; default manual Fresh Install proof remains empty-target-only and returns BLOCK for the occupied database.

An explicit manual opt-in can only select the exact dedicated disposable project identity, validated over TLS and through full known-schema, catalog, cross-schema, Auth and Storage preconditions before proposed cleanup.

The controlled reprovision transaction proves a clean application schema, applies exactly the 59 canonical customer-baseline SQL files, restores Auth bootstrap and neutral seed, and validates target postflight before committing.

Fault injection before cleanup, during the migration chain, during Auth bootstrap, during postflight and on connection loss produces a BLOCKED proof and leaves the old schema intact when PostgreSQL rollback is available.
Exact-head GitHub evidence distinguishes occupied-target reproducible replay from a truly virgin provider environment; authenticated Alap/Pro role and RLS behaviors remain separately required.
unresolvedRisks: PostgreSQL schema DROP CASCADE can remove cross-schema Auth triggers and non-application dependent objects; all such dependencies must be explicitly enumerated, denied unless approved, and restored or their loss causes rollback.
Supabase Storage buckets are provider-managed and existing migration scripts upsert bucket metadata; evidence cannot honestly assert all-provider pristine state after an application schema reset.
The true database-URL TLS identity and transaction semantics can only be proven in a separate controlled hosted execution, not in mocked or static CI.
Operational interruption or competing traffic during schema reset could break transactional assumptions; serialization and exclusivity controls need validated proof.

in: Build strict guarded disposable-only *optional* app-schema reprovision into the existing Fresh Install proof workflow, rather than creating a second deployment authority.

Validate immutable reviewed baseline source, expected occupied-schema catalog fingerprint and known-only noncustomer catalog rows, zero Auth/Storage user data, managed buckets and external dependencies.
Implement bounded PostgreSQL atomic cleanup plus canonical 59-file replay, auth-bootstrap, neutral seed and final postflight; treat any failure as rollback.
Add fixture-based hostile tests covering wrong project, source tamper, data drift, managed schema changes, concurrent invocation and rollback/failure semantics.
Keep all execution manual, exact-project opt-in with evidence, and preserve all existing gates including tenant/plan signed-in RLS as separate future proof.
out: No automatic PR/push/scheduled or Vercel-triggered destructive database action; no undocumented bypass of target-preflight or privileged user data guards.
No reset of waterk-platform, paused waterk-staging, any non-disposable database or Supabase managed Auth/Storage/realtime internal schemas.
No changes to customer data, actual production migrations, paid projects, billing configuration, template factory or VX Builder.
No completion claim for authenticated Office Alap/Pro roles or full customer acceptance based solely on schema replay.

requirements.requirement: The existing Fresh Install workflow must preserve its non-destructive default and make hosted schema cleanup possible only through a separately authorized exact disposable-target manual dispatch.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Untrusted push, pull request or default input triggers schema deletion.

requirements.requirement: A typed, exact-source reprovision procedure must fail closed on schema or user-data drift, and any failed migration must roll back the intended cleanup rather than leave partial installation.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Failed migration or Auth bootstrap commits emptied or inconsistent schema.

requirements.requirement: Source-only and CI evidence cannot claim hosted 59-migration replay success, Alap/Pro signed-in Office behavior or full provider Fresh Install readiness without independently observed target proof.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A preflight-only or fixture-based test becomes a claimed hosted database proof.
